sentences.text: Scientists know three distinct species of Igdabatis from the Cretaceous period.
The genus Igdabatis was first described by Cappella in 1972.
Igdabatis is classified within the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish.
It belongs to the family Myliobatidae.
The type species of the genus Igdabatis is Igdabatis sigmodon.
This animal lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, spanning from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
Fossils appear in Maastrichtian rocks in Spain, the Dukamaje Formation of Niger, and various formations in India.
